summary: The Jewish exiles return to Jerusalem under Persian King Cyrus's decree to rebuild the temple and walls, facing opposition but guided by leaders like Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah. They restore temple worship, confront challenges, and renew their commitment to God's law through scripture study.

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.note: Son of Shealtiel. With Jeshua he rebuilt the altar and began the temple in Jerusalem, and he refused the offer of help from the people who opposed the work (Ezra 3:8; 4:3; 5:2).

people.name: Ezra
people.note: Priest and scribe who led a group of exiles to Jerusalem, emphasized scripture study, and helped the people repent (Ezra 7:1–6; Nehemiah 8:1).

people.name: Nehemiah
people.note: Cupbearer to King Artaxerxes who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls despite opposition; relied on God for strength (Nehemiah 2:1, 4:14).

people.name: Sanballat and Tobiah
people.note: Opponents of the Jews who mocked and hindered the rebuilding efforts (Nehemiah 2:19; 4:1).

people.name: Sheshbazzar
people.note: Prince of Judah appointed to oversee the temple's reconstruction and receive returned sacred vessels (Ezra 1:8; 5:14).

locations.name: Jerusalem
locations.note: The city where the temple and walls were rebuilt; central to the Jews' religious and cultural identity (Ezra 1:3; Nehemiah 2:3).

locations.name: Temple in Jerusalem
locations.note: Rebuilt under Zerubbabel's leadership; dedicated with sacrifices and joyous celebrations (Ezra 3:10; 6:16–18).

locations.name: Wall of Jerusalem
locations.note: Rebuilt by Nehemiah despite opposition; completed in 52 days through diligent labor and faith (Nehemiah 4:6; 6:15).

locations.name: Water Gate
locations.note: Location where Ezra read the law to the people, fostering spiritual renewal (Nehemiah 8:1–2).

background: After 70 years of Babylonian captivity, the Jews returned to Jerusalem under Persian rule. They faced challenges like opposition from neighboring groups, economic hardship, and the need to restore religious practices. Leaders like Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah guided the restoration of the temple, walls, and covenantal commitments, emphasizing faith, perseverance, and scripture.

manualHighlights.note: God inspires leaders like Cyrus, Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah to accomplish His work, even amid opposition (Jeremiah 29:10; Isaiah 44:28).
The temple's reconstruction and the study of the law (Nehemiah 8) symbolize spiritual renewal; the Lord's house and His word bring joy and strength.
Nehemiah's response to opposition—prayer, vigilance, and trust in God—exemplifies how to handle challenges in the Lord's work (Nehemiah 4:6, 9; 6:3).
